chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Manqari, from Isa ibn Yunus, from al-Awza'i, from al-Zuhri, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both).

In the case of a man who claimed against his wife that he married her with a guardian and witnesses, and the wife denied this, and her sister presented evidence against this man that he married her with a guardian and witnesses, and did not specify a time: that the evidence is the husband's evidence and the wife's evidence is not accepted, because the husband has already acquired the right to the intimacy of this woman, and her sister wants the dissolution of the marriage, so she is not verified and her evidence is not accepted unless with a specified time before her time or consummation with her.

key_terms.بُضْع: Intimacy/consummation; the right to sexual relations within marriage
key_terms.شُهُودٍ: Witnesses; those who attest to the marriage contract
key_terms.وَلِيٍّ: Guardian; the male relative who officiates the marriage contract

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for accepting the wife's side's evidence in a marriage contract dispute according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in Shia jurisprudence, where the husband's established right to intimacy (*budh*) creates a default presumption of marriage validity unless overturned. It highlights the evidentiary asymmetry in marital disputes, requiring the wife's side to provide specific temporal evidence or proof of consummation to rebut the husband's claim, reflecting the juristic focus on stabilizing family structures.
